## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: copilot
body:
Web app that auto-detects browser geolocation, pulls real-time weather + soil data, and predicts rice crop yield via a trained ML model.

## Backend (`app.py` — Flask)
- `POST /api/analyze` — takes `{lat, lon, area_acres?}`; reverse-geocodes via Nominatim, fetches weather from Open-Meteo, infers soil type/moisture by region, determines Kharif/Rabi/Zaid season, runs Random Forest prediction → returns `yield_per_acre_kg` + `yield_per_hectare_tons`
- `POST /api/calculate` — `yield_per_acre × area_acres` → total kg + tons + hectares
- Random Forest (200 trees, scikit-learn) trained on 5,000 synthetic samples at startup; model cached as `yield_model.pkl`; thread-safe singleton load
- All external calls (Nominatim, Open-Meteo) fail gracefully with sensible defaults

## Frontend
- `templates/index.html` — single-page UI: location trigger → coordinate/weather/soil cards → ML prediction highlight → yield calculator
- `static/css/style.css` — responsive agricultural-themed layout; CSS custom properties, grid card system
- `static/js/main.js` — `navigator.geolocation` → `POST /api/analyze` → render; separate calculator hits `POST /api/calculate`

## Model features
| Feature | Source |
|---|---|
| Temperature, Rainfall, Humidity | Open-Meteo (30-day window) |
| Soil type (encoded), Soil moisture | Region-inferred from state/lat |
| Season | Calendar month → Kharif/Rabi/Zaid |
| Historical district yield | Representative constant (2800 kg/acre) |

## Summary

Add many-to-many compatibility relationship between protocols and macros, manageable from both directions across creation, settings, and overview pages, plus flow builder integration.

## Where compatibility can be managed

### Protocol → Macro
- **Protocol creation page**: select compatible macros during protocol creation via a search dropdown
- **Protocol settings page**: link and unlink compatible macros via a search dropdown
- **Protocol overview page**: read-only display of compatible macros

### Macro → Protocol
- **Macro creation page**: select compatible protocols during macro creation via a search dropdown
- **Macro settings page**: link and unlink compatible protocols via a search dropdown
- **Macro overview page**: read-only display of compatible protocols

### Flow builder
- **Analysis node**: when a protocol is selected upstream, compatible macros appear first in the dropdown with a badge
- **Warning**: selecting an incompatible macro shows a warning banner

## Changes Made

### Database
- `protocolMacros` join table with composite PK and cascade deletes

### API (`packages/api`)
- Schema: `zCompatibleMacroSummary`, `zProtocolMacroEntry`, `zAddCompatibleMacrosBody`, etc.
- Contract: list/add/remove compatible macros on protocols, list/add/remove compatible protocols on macros
- OpenAPI spec regenerated

### Backend (`apps/backend`)
- **Protocol → Macro direction**: `ProtocolMacroRepository`, `ListCompatibleMacrosUseCase`, `AddCompatibleMacrosUseCase`, `RemoveCompatibleMacroUseCase`, controller handlers
- **Macro → Protocol direction**: `MacroProtocolRepository`, `ListCompatibleProtocolsUseCase`, `AddCompatibleProtocolsUseCase`, `RemoveCompatibleProtocolUseCase`, controller handlers

### Frontend (`apps/web`)

The existing Reddington's Theatre was a generic two-storey box with no recognisable theatre silhouette. This rewrite of `CUSTOM_BUILDERS['reddingtons']` transforms it into a convincing Art Deco West End theatre.

### Massing — depth 2.8 → 6.0 across four distinct zones

| Zone | Depth | Height | Material |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ornate facade | 1.8 | 2.9 + stepped parapet | Cream stone `#F5F5DC` |
| Auditorium | 2.2 | 2.8 + barrel vault | Brick `#8B4513` |
| Fly tower | 1.2 | **6.0** (windowless) | Brick `#8B4513` |
| Backstage | 0.8 | 1.5 | Brick `#8B4513` |

### Art Deco facade
- **Stepped parapet** — 5-section profile: centre → 4.2, mid → 3.8, outer → 3.4; gold cap trim + spire finials
- **8 fluted pilasters** (4 per side, clear of entrance) with gold capitals and brick groove lines
- **Double-row chevron friezes** in antique gold `#D4AF37` at the floor division

### Entrance & marquee
- Wide theatrical-red canopy (`W=2.2`), 12 amber spherical bulbs along front edge, diagonal gold brackets
- Enlarged **sunburst motif**: 20 alternating gold/brass rays, radius 0.72
- Large burgundy show banner (`H=0.78`) with 3 staggered rows of gold bar lettering for *OCTOCATS CODE*

### Street details
- A-frame poster boards flanking entrance with coloured poster strips and foliage planters
- Brass velvet rope posts with deep red connecting rope
- **Stage door** on left side wall near fly tower junction, with brass sign above

### Fly tower
The defining change — a tall windowless brick monolith (`H=6.0`) rising dramatically above all other elements, producing the unmistakable theatre silhouette visible across the village.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


----

*This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

<issue_title>Planning permission: Extend Reddington's Theatre to be a convincing West End theatre</issue_title>
<issue_description>### What changes do you want?

The current Reddington's theatre building looks like a generic two-storey commercial building, not a London West End theatre venue.

### Required Changes

**1. Increase the depth significantly** — change `D` from 2.8 to approximately 5.5–6.0. A theatre is much deeper than it is wide to accommodate front-of-house, auditorium, stage, and backstage areas. The building should have clearly distinct massing zones from front to back:
   - **Front section** (ornate facade, entrance, FOH): The decorated public face, roughly 1.5–2.0 units deep.
   - **Auditorium section** (mid-height, wider volume behind FOH): The main seating block, roughly 2.0–2.5 units deep, slightly lower roofline than the front facade but taller than a single storey.
   - **Stage/Fly tower** (tall, plain rectangular tower): Rising 1.5–2× the height of the front facade, windowless, set back from the front. This is the most important element — it's what makes a building recognisable as a theatre. Roughly 1.0–1.5 units deep.
   - **Backstage block** (low, utilitarian rear section): Plain, lower than the auditorium, with a stage door on one side wall.

**2. Add a proper fly tower** — A tall, windowless rectangular block rising above the stage area, clearly taller than the front facade. Use plain brick material (not the ornate front stone). This is the defining silhouette feature of any theatre.

**3. Redesign the entrance with a proper marquee canopy** — Replace the current flat black box with a thinner, wider canopy that projects out over the entrance steps. Add small spherical "bulb" geometries along its front edge to suggest theatre-style lighting. Support it with thin decorative brackets.

**4. Strengthen the Art Deco styling on the facade**:
   - Make the front parapet **stepped** — higher in the centre, stepping down symmetrically to each side (a classic Art Deco silhouette).
   - Add **chevron/zigzag friezes** between floors using small triangular or V-shaped box primitives in gold material.
   - Enlarge the **sunburst/fan motif** above the entrance — make it a prominent decorative centrepiece spanning at least half the facade width, using wedge-shaped geometries radiating from a central point.
   - Add **fluted vertical pilaster strips** running the full height of the facade for strong verticality.
   - Use more **gold/brass material** trim — Art Deco is bold and glamorous.

**5. Improve the show banner** — Create a larger, more prominent banner/sign area. Use a tall, rich red or deep purple rectangular panel on the upper facade with a larger-scale geometric arrangement of gold-coloured box primitives suggesting the title "Octocats Code". The banner should be immediately eye-catching even at distance.

**6. Add flanking poster boards** — Place two small A-frame poster board structures (flat rectangular panels on thin legs) on either side of the entrance steps, like the show posters you see outside every West End theatre.

**7. Add a stage door** — Place a small, understated door on one side wall (left or right) near the rear of the building, with a small horizontal sign-like element above it. This is an iconic feature of any theatre.

**8. Add an auditorium roof profile** — The section over the auditorium (between FOH and fly tower) should have a slightly different roofline — either a gentle barrel-vault (curved) using a half-cylinder geometry, or a simple pitched/gabled roof. This distinguishes it from the flat-roofed FOH and the tall fly tower.

### Style Reference

Think of theatres like the **Trafalgar Theatre** (Art Deco, restored 2021), **Apollo Victoria**, or **Noël Coward Theatre** — bold geometric decoration on the facade, a prominent entrance canopy, and a clearly visible fly tower rising above the rest of the building.

author: sfc-gh-relshenawy
body:
# Fix Broken Table of Contents Links in Rendered Documentation

## Description & Motivation

In the documentation output by `scripts/render_journey.py`, some Table of Contents (TOC) links don't redirect to the relevant section. This is because the TOC and the document body were using **different sources** for step titles, producing mismatched anchor IDs.

Three root causes were identified:

1. **Title source mismatch** -- The TOC (`generate_table_of_contents()`) reads titles from `meta.yaml`, but the document body (`render_blueprint_guidance()` / `render_blueprint_code()`) used `get_step_title()` which reads from `dynamic.md.jinja`. When a jinja template has no `# ` title line, the body falls back to the raw step slug, producing a different anchor than the TOC.
2. **Divergent titles** -- Some steps have different human-readable titles in `meta.yaml` vs their `dynamic.md.jinja` template (e.g., "Create Organization Account Administrators" vs "Create Account Administrators"), causing anchor mismatches.
3. **Special character handling** -- Characters like `&`, `,`, `()` in titles are stripped by `generate_anchor()`. This is fine as long as both TOC and body use the same title string, but the bugs above meant they often didn't.

**Fix:** Introduced a `resolve_step_title()` function that establishes `meta.yaml` as the single source of truth for step titles (matching what the TOC already uses), with fallback to jinja template title, then to the slug. All four call sites in `render_blueprint_guidance()` and `render_blueprint_code()` now use this function, ensuring TOC and body anchors always match.

## Ticket

[CXE-14541](https://snowflakecomputing.atlassian.net/browse/CXE-14541) -- "Some table of contents links don't work"

- Parent: [CXE-14390](https://snowflakecomputing.atlassian.net/browse/CXE-14390) -- M2: Checklist to make Blueprints repo public
- Epic: [CXE-14156](https://snowflakecomputing.atlassian.net/browse/CXE-14156) -- M2: Select customers and SI partners using Blueprints directly

## Changes

### `scripts/render_journey.py`
- Added `resolve_step_title(step_id, step_path, task_context)` -- canonical title resolution with priority: meta.yaml title > jinja `# ` title > slug.
- Updated all four step-title resolution sites in `render_blueprint_code()` (skip header + normal header) and `render_blueprint_guidance()` (skip header + normal header) to use `resolve_step_title()` instead of the previous inline `get_step_title()` / slug fallback logic.

### `scripts/test_render_journey.py`
- Added `TestResolveStepTitle` (7 tests) -- unit tests for the new `resolve_step_title()` function covering: meta.yaml preferred over jinja, fallback to jinja when meta is empty, fallback to slug when neither has a title, no task_context scenarios, and step-not-found-in-context fallback.
- Added `TestTocToHeadingAnchorConsistency` (5 tests) -- integration tests verifying that TOC anchors match body heading anchors for: divergent jinja/meta titles (Bug 2), missing jinja titles (Bug 1), `&` in titles (Bug 3), commas and special characters, and task-level anchors.

## Local Testing

- All existing tests pass (`python -m pytest scripts/test_render_journey.py`).
- 12 new tests pass, covering all three bugs and edge cases.
- Manual verification: rendered output for steps with known mismatches (e.g., `configure-scim-integration`, `create-organization-account-administrators`, `define-domains-environments-and-object-naming-conventions`) now produces matching TOC-to-heading anchors.

## How to Test / Review

1. Run the full test suite:
   ```bash
   python -m pytest scripts/test_render_journey.py -v
   ```
2. Focus on the new tests:
   ```bash
   python -m pytest scripts/test_render_journey.py -v -k "TestResolveStepTitle or TestTocToHeadingAnchorConsistency"
   ```
3. Optionally render a blueprint with known mismatches (e.g., `platform-foundation-setup`) and verify that all TOC links navigate to the correct sections in the output markdown.

## Config / Migration Steps

None. This is a pure code change with no configuration, migration, or environment changes.

## Breaking Changes

None. The external behavior is corrected (TOC links now work), but no APIs, CLI interfaces, or configuration formats are changed.

author: sid-qin
body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** pnpm and bun use content-addressable stores where every installed file is a hardlink (`nlink > 1`). The `rejectHardlinks` check (defaulting to `true`) in `openBoundaryFileSync` rejects **all** plugin manifests and entry points, making every plugin unusable when OpenClaw is installed via pnpm.
- **Why it matters:** All pnpm users on v2026.2.26 cannot start the gateway — 35+ bundled extensions fail with `unsafe plugin manifest path`. This affects both Linux (WSL2) and Windows users.
- **What changed:** Added package manager store path detection (`node_modules/.pnpm/`, `.bun/install/cache/`) in `openBoundaryFileSync`. When the canonical (resolved) path is inside a known package manager store, the hardlink check is skipped. Also added `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_ALLOW_HARDLINKS=true` env var as an escape hatch.
- **What did NOT change:** No call-site modifications. All 5 `openBoundaryFileSync` call sites in the plugin system remain untouched. The hardlink check still applies to user-writable plugin directories (e.g. `~/.openclaw/plugins/`).

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #28122
- Closes #28175
- Alternative to #28527

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Plugins now load correctly when OpenClaw is installed via pnpm or bun
- No change for npm/yarn users (files have `nlink=1`, check is a no-op)
- New env var `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_ALLOW_HARDLINKS=true` available as escape hatch for uncovered package managers

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`

### Security Analysis

The hardlink-escape attack requires an attacker to create a hardlink from inside a plugin directory to a sensitive file outside it. The boundary path check (`resolveBoundaryPathSync`) cannot distinguish hardlinks from regular files since both resolve to the same canonical path.

This fix preserves the hardlink check for **user-writable directories** where the attack is possible, and only skips it for **read-only package manager store paths** (`node_modules/.pnpm/`) where:
1. Files are created by the package manager, not by users
2. The store is not a user-writable attack surface
3. Hardlinks are the expected, intended state

All 3 existing hardlink security tests pass unchanged because they use temp directories (not pnpm store paths).

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS (dev), Linux WSL2 + Windows (affected users)
- Runtime: Node.js v22+
- Package manager: pnpm v10.x

### Steps

1. Install OpenClaw via pnpm: `pnpm add -g openclaw@2026.2.26`
2. Run `openclaw gateway`

### Expected

- All bundled plugins load successfully

### Actual

- Before fix: All 35+ plugins rejected with `unsafe plugin manifest path (validation)`
- After fix: Plugins load normally; hardlink security checks still active for user-writable paths

## Evidence

All 34 plugin tests pass (23 loader + 11 discovery), including the 3 hardlink security tests:

```
✓ rejects plugin entry files that escape plugin root via hardlink
✓ rejects package extension entries that are hardlinked aliases
✓ ignores package manifests that are hardlinked aliases
```

TypeScript compilation: zero errors.

### Why this approach over PR #28527

| Dimension | PR #28527 (disable everywhere) | This PR (smart detection) |
|-----------|:---:|:---:|
| pnpm manifest loading | Fixed | Fixed |
| pnpm entry point loading | Fixed | Fixed |
| User-writable dir security | **Lost** | **Preserved** |
| Existing 3 security tests | **All fail** | **All pass** |
| Files changed | 4 files, 5 call sites | **1 file, 0 call sites** |
| Future call sites auto-covered | No | **Yes** |

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: All 34 plugin tests (loader + discovery) pass
- Edge cases checked: hardlink escape via temp dir still rejected; pnpm store path detection works cross-platform (normalized with forward slashes)
- What I did **not** verify: Actual pnpm global install on Linux/Windows (no pnpm global env available; relying on path-based detection logic and reporter confirmation from #28122/#28175)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No` (new optional env var only)
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert: Revert this single commit, or set `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_ALLOW_HARDLINKS=false` (default behavior)
- Files/config to restore: `src/infra/boundary-file-read.ts`
- Known bad symptoms: If detection is too narrow, pnpm plugins fail with `unsafe plugin manifest path`; if too broad, hardlink attacks in user-writable dirs could bypass the check

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk:** An attacker creates a `.pnpm` directory inside a user-writable plugin path to bypass the check. **Mitigation:** The attacker already needs write access to the plugin directory; if they have that, they can place malicious code directly without needing a hardlink escape. The boundary path check still enforces containment.
- **Risk:** Unknown package managers with hardlinks not covered by path detection. **Mitigation:** `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_ALLOW_HARDLINKS=true` env var provides an immediate workaround.

body:
Enables users to drill into invitation leagues from the profile pane, compare predicted points across all opponents, and view any opponent's team formation directly.

## Backend

- **New endpoint** `GET /api/leagues-classic/:leagueId/standings?gameweeksAhead=N` — fetches FPL classic league standings and enriches each entry with cumulative predicted points across 1–5 future gameweeks. Bench players (multiplier = 0) are correctly excluded from the prediction sum.
- Added `validateLeagueId()` to `validation.js` and `fetchLeagueStandings()` to `dataProvider.js` (supports mock mode).
- Added `backend/mockData/league-standings.json` for test/mock usage.

```
GET /api/leagues-classic/12345/standings?gameweeksAhead=3
→ { league, standings: { results: [{ ..., predicted_points: 98.4 }] }, currentGameweek, gameweeksAhead }
```

## Frontend

- **`InvitationLeagueView`** — new sidebar component showing a standings table with rank change icons, GW points, total points, and a **1–5 GW toggle** for the predicted points column. Team names are clickable.
- **`UserProfilePane`** — invitation league names are now clickable buttons; fires `onLeagueClick(league)` prop.
- **`App.js`** — coordinates the new flows:
  - Clicking a league replaces the profile pane with `InvitationLeagueView`
  - Clicking a team name loads that opponent's formation with a "Viewing opponent's team / Back to My Team" banner; hides Recommended Transfers while viewing an opponent

### Motivation

- Ensure ASPF opportunity identities are derived from canonical ASPF carrier tuples (NodeId/fingerprint) rather than opaque hash prefixes for clearer, stable identity and easier downstream validation. 
- Treat structure-class digests as auxiliary compatibility metadata while making the NodeId-backed canonical identity the primary structural carrier.

### Description

- Changed `OpportunityDecisionProtocol` to include an explicit `canonical_identity` JSON payload and an optional `opportunity_hash` compatibility field, and emit `canonical_identity` in `as_row()` and `as_rewrite_plan()` outputs. 
- Reworked reusable-boundary opportunity IDs to be derived from the canonical `NodeId` components (e.g. `Opportunity:ReusableBoundaryRepresentative` + representative key) instead of using the prior hash-prefix scheme, while preserving the short hash as `opportunity_hash`. 
- Added helper `_node_id_identity_payload(node_id: NodeId)` to produce `node_id` + `node_fingerprint` payloads used as canonical identity carriers. 
- Updated `AspfStructureClass` so `canonical_identity` (NodeId + fingerprint + child fingerprints) is the primary payload and `digest()` is retained as an auxiliary compatibility field in `structure_class_payload()`. 
- Updated tests to assert the new canonical identity fields and compatibility hash behavior in rewrite-plan outputs (`tests/test_aspf_visitors.py`).

author: copilot
body:
Visiting the User Profile page after saving rich text content would immediately show "You have unsaved changes" and block navigation with a confirmation prompt — without the user editing anything.

## Root Cause

Two compounding issues:

1. **`UserProfile.vue`** initialized `formData` with `''` and deferred the store value assignment to `onMounted`. Because child components mount before parents, `RichTextEditor` was already alive with empty content when `onMounted` fired and updated the prop — triggering the editor's prop watcher.

2. **`RichTextEditor.vue`** called `setContent(value, false)` expecting TipTap 2.x semantics where the second arg suppresses `onUpdate`. In TipTap 3.x this no longer reliably prevents the emission, so `onUpdate` fired with a potentially normalized HTML string that differed from the stored value — producing the false positive.

## Changes

- **`UserProfile.vue`**: Initialize `formData` directly from the store at declaration time. Pinia stores are synchronously available (they call `loadFromStorage()` immediately), so `onMounted` was unnecessary. This eliminates the prop change on mount and prevents the watcher from needing to fire `setContent` at all.

  ```js
  // Before
  const formData = ref({ professionalExperience: '' })
  onMounted(() => { formData.value = { professionalExperience: professionalExperience.value || '' } })

  // After
  const formData = ref({ professionalExperience: professionalExperience.value || '' })
  ```

- **`RichTextEditor.vue`**: Add an `isSettingContent` guard flag that suppresses `onUpdate` emissions while a programmatic `setContent` is in flight. Defensive measure against TipTap 3.x firing `onUpdate` regardless of the `emitUpdate` parameter.

author: copilot
body:
No health check endpoint existed, blocking load balancer configuration and availability alerting. Adds `GET /health` (public, no auth) that checks PostgreSQL and S3 connectivity.

## Changes

### `src/modules/health/`
- **`health.module.ts`** — wires `TerminusModule`, controller, and S3 indicator
- **`health.controller.ts`** — `GET /health` decorated with `@Public()` and `@HealthCheck()`; runs `TypeOrmHealthIndicator.pingCheck` + custom S3 check
- **`indicators/s3-health.indicator.ts`** — extends `HealthIndicator`; uses `HeadBucketCommand` to probe bucket reachability; returns unhealthy (not throws) when bucket or credentials are absent

### `src/app.module.ts`
- Registers `HealthModule`

## Example response

```json
// 200 OK — all healthy
{
  "status": "ok",
  "info": {
    "database": { "status": "up" },
    "s3": { "status": "up" }
  },
  "error": {},
  "details": { "database": { "status": "up" }, "s3": { "status": "up" } }
}

// 503 Service Unavailable — partial failure
{
  "status": "error",
  "info": { "database": { "status": "up" } },
  "error": { "s3": { "status": "down", "message": "..." } },
  "details": { ... }
}
```

body:
## What changes were made
- Updated [`crates/relay-tunnel/Cargo.lock`](crates/relay-tunnel/Cargo.lock) to sync the local `api-types` path dependency version from `0.1.19` to `0.1.20`.
- No source code behavior changes; this is a lockfile consistency fix.

## Why these changes were made
- The relay image build in remote deployment CI failed on February 27, 2026 (run `22498655753`, job `65179704494`) during:
  - `cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path crates/relay-tunnel/Cargo.toml --features server`
- Failure reason: Cargo needed to mutate `crates/relay-tunnel/Cargo.lock`, but `--locked` forbids lockfile updates.
- Root cause: the `api-types` crate version had been bumped to `0.1.20`, while `crates/relay-tunnel/Cargo.lock` still referenced `0.1.19`.

## Important implementation details
- This fix keeps the existing strict `--locked` build behavior intact (instead of weakening build guarantees by changing build flags).
- The lockfile now reflects the current dependency graph for `crates/relay-tunnel`.
- Validation performed:
  - `cargo build --locked --manifest-path crates/relay-tunnel/Cargo.toml --features server`
  - `cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path crates/relay-tunnel/Cargo.toml --features server`

### Motivation
- Preserve per-sample CD and LER measurements to enable per-image distributions and per-sample exports rather than only aggregate statistics.
- Provide a UI to choose which sample's histogram to view and generate per-sample plot files for download.
- Improve UX around live refresh during runs and make overlay/design upload state handling more robust.

### Description
- Store per-sample arrays in session state with new keys `cd_samples_by_sample`, `ler_samples_by_sample`, `ler_is_summary_by_sample`, `last_completed_sample_id`, `hist_selected_sample_id`, and `live_refresh_enabled`, and sanitize sample IDs for plot filenames via new helper `_plot_sample_suffix`.
- Update result handling to record per-sample CD and LER arrays (including fallback to summary LER), set last completed sample, and persist per-image JSON/CSV files under the run directory.
- Replace single aggregate histograms with a selectable `Histogram dataset` `selectbox` that shows per-sample CD/LER histograms and still produces aggregate histograms, and generate PNG bytes for per-sample and aggregate plots stored in `st.session_state.plot_bytes` for zipping/download.
- Adjust UI controls: add keys for design upload inputs and clear them when not used, increase `bootstrap_iters` defaults/range and add hints/captions, remove the old `live_refresh` toggle and instead enable live refresh only while a run is starting/active, and ensure `live_refresh_enabled` is cleared on stop/error/done.

⚡ Bolt: Optimize iCal property writing

💡 **What:** Refactored `write_property_impl` to process text in chunks using `str::find` and `push_str` instead of iterating character-by-character.
🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation was CPU-intensive due to repeated bounds checking and allocation overhead for every single character.
📊 **Impact:** Reduces execution time for writing large properties by ~42% (~145ms -> ~84ms in benchmarks).
🔬 **Measurement:** Verified with `cargo test -p api --lib -- --ignored benchmark_write_property_impl` (benchmark added during development, removed before commit). Confirmed correctness with existing iCalendar unit tests.

## Summary
This PR reduces allocation churn in the core layout/render hot paths without changing rendering behavior.

### Changes in scope
- `packages/core/src/layout/engine/layoutEngine.ts`

- `packages/core/src/layout/engine/pool.ts`

body:
### Motivation

- Mejorar la detección/selección de dispositivos USB en Java usando la API nativa de Android y soportar flujos con múltiples dispositivos conectados.
- Asegurar que los nombres de soname versionados se resuelvan en runtime en Android cuando los binarios en `jniLibs` usan nombres compatibles con la plataforma.
- Hacer más robusta la extracción de assets críticos (`pci.ids(.gz)`) y la preparación de enlaces/copia de librerías y binarios en el sandbox.
- Hacer idempotente y más tolerante el script de parche de `libusb` para inyectar el uso de `ANDROID_USB_FD`.

### Description

- Añade enumeración directa con `UsbManager.getDeviceList()` y un selector UI para elegir entre múltiples dispositivos, solicita permiso y abre `UsbDevice` para extraer el FD y usarlo en native; se creó `formatUsbDeviceLabel`, `requestUsbPermission` y flujo de selección en `MainActivity` y se registró el broadcast con `ContextCompat.registerReceiver`.
- Agrega acción de menú `action_programmer` y UI para configurar/seleccionar el programador de `flashrom`, además de mejoras en el diálogo "Acerca de" y comprobaciones de importación de archivos con validación de `InputStream` nulo.
- Refactoriza `AssetHelper` para soportar que `pci.ids.gz` aparezca en assets como `pci.ids`, añade `copyCriticalPciIds`, tratamiento especial en `copyAssetFile` y lógica mejorada de enlaces para resolver sonames Android-compat (`libz_1.so`, `libcrypto_3.so`, `libssl_3.so`) con `linkRuntimeSoname`, `resolveNativeLibrary` y `getNativeCandidates`.
- Actualiza `ensureNativeToolLinks` para crear symlinks (o copia) de ejecutables y librerías runtime hacia `jniLibs` y obliga a la presencia de dependencias críticas (`libconfuse.so`, `libz.so.1`, `libc++_shared.so`), además de exponer utilidades para encontrar el origen nativo en logs (`findNativeName`).
- Elimina la dependencia de `usb-serial-for-android` en `app/build.gradle` y actualiza la documentación (`README.md`, `AUDITORIA_ANDROID_RUNTIME.md`, `MATRIZ_RUNTIME.md`, `REPORTE_DEPENDENCIAS_BINARIOS.md`) para reflejar la nueva estrategia de enumeración USB, renombrado de sonames y el estado runtime.
- Mejora `patch_libusb.py` para lectura/escritura con `utf-8`, aplicar cambios de forma idempotente mediante detección previa, insertar headers y snippets en anclas más tolerantes y reportar estado cuando ya está parcheado.

### Testing

- Ejecutado `./gradlew assembleDebug` para validar el empaquetado y la integración de `jniLibs` y la tarea completó correctamente.
- Ejecutado `./gradlew test` para tareas de unit tests; la tarea se completó y no había tests unitarios adicionales configurados que fallaran.
- Verificación manual de flujo lógico en logs: la app ahora informa la presencia/origen de `libcrypto.so.3`, `libssl.so.3` y `libz.so.1` en runtime y copia/normaliza `pci.ids.gz` cuando aparece como `pci.ids` en assets.

author: alinawaz258
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a complete, production-style AI-powered urban flood defense system for Chennai that uses GCP free-tier primitives (BigQuery ML / TimesFM via `AI.FORECAST`) to forecast rainfall and drive downstream flood risk, routing, emergency deployment and road clearance decisions exposed via an API and simple frontend.
- Make the system resilient to offline/constrained environments by providing mock fallbacks so the service and UI remain testable even when cloud client libraries are unavailable.

### Description
- Reorganized and implemented a modular backend under `backend/app/` with typed Pydantic schemas (`app/models/schemas.py`) and services: `bigquery_service.py`, `risk_engine.py`, `routing_service.py`, `deployment_service.py`, `clearance_service.py`, and `system_service.py` that encapsulate forecasting, risk scoring, network routing, assignment optimization and clearance prioritization. 
- Exposed the orchestration via a FastAPI app (`backend/main.py`) with endpoints `GET /forecast`, `GET /forecast/sql`, `GET /zones`, `POST /route`, `POST /deploy`, and `POST /simulate` and produced a reusable `sql/rainfall_forecast_timesfm.sql` that runs TimesFM `AI.FORECAST` for a 7-day horizon. 
- Implemented routing using `networkx` where edge weight = `Base_Distance + (Flood_Probability * 100) + (Water_Depth * 50)` and edges with `Water_Depth > 20cm` are marked blocked, with A* as primary and Dijkstra as fallback via `RoutingEngine.get_safe_route`. 
- Implemented emergency deployment optimization using the Hungarian algorithm (`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment`) in `EmergencyDeploymentService`, road clearance prioritization with volume/pump-time/priority score in `RoadClearanceService`, and a simulation flow in `FloodDefenseService.simulate` that applies a rainfall multiplier and recomputes routes, dispatch and clearance. 
- Added a simple production-ready frontend (`frontend/index.html`) in vanilla JS to display a mocked risk heatmap, route panel, emergency dispatch table and a rainfall-simulation slider wired to the backend. 
- Added safe BigQuery client handling and offline fallbacks: `bigquery` and `service_account` imports are optional so `BigQueryRepository` will use local mock data when cloud libraries or credentials are not available, plus a standalone runner `backend/run_forecast.py` and `requirements.txt` updated for the stack. 

### Testing
- Compiled the backend to validate syntax with `python -m compileall backend` which completed successfully. 
- Performed service-level smoke checks by running `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=backend python - <<'PY' ...` that instantiated `FloodDefenseService` and exercised `forecast()`, `zone_risk()`, `route()` and `deploy()` paths successfully using mock data. 
- Launched the backend and static server then captured a frontend screenshot via an automated browser script (Playwright) which completed and produced `artifacts/dashboard.png`. 
- Dependency installation and full integration tests were partially blocked by the environment (proxy prevented installation of `google-cloud-bigquery`), and `fastapi.testclient` checks failed in this environment because `httpx` was not installed, so full end-to-end cloud integration tests against actual BigQuery were not run here.

**Problem:**
When opening or closing a POS session, chatter messages display untranslated English text regardless of the user's language setting.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Set user language to any non-English language (e.g., Spanish)
2. Open a POS session and register cash in/out operations
3. Close the session
4. Check the chatter messages - labels appear in English

**Current behavior:**
Messages display in English: "Opening cash difference", "Opening cash expected", "Opening cash counted", "Closing difference", etc.

**Expected behavior:**
Messages should be translated according to the user's language setting.

**Cause of the issue:**
The hardcoded strings were not wrapped in the translation function `_()`, preventing them from being translated.

**Fix:**
Wrap the concatenated strings with `_()` to enable proper translation of all cash details messages.

For configurations that use rook-ceph, the mon, mgr, and chassis placement labels are mandatory.

If Deployment Manager is configured without the labels ceph-mgr-placement: enabled, ceph-mon-placement: enabled, and the required chassis label (for example, topology.rook.io/chassis: "group-0") defined in the deployment-config.yaml of the Host Custom Resource, the system will complete initialization and reach an online state. However, the Deployment Manager will report INSYNC=false.

These labels are required to ensure proper placement of Ceph MON and MGR pods and to maintain alignment between the Deployment Manager and the underlying Rook-Ceph topology. Without them, the cluster may appear operational, but it will remain in a degraded synchronization state from the Deployment Manager perspective.

author: dglazkov
body:
## What

Restructures context caching in the agent loop to cache the static envelope
(system instruction + tools) separately from conversation contents, and adds
progressive cache refreshes for long-running agent loops.

## Why

The original implementation rebuilt static fields every turn and cached
everything (including the objective) on turn 0, causing duplication on
subsequent turns. Short runs ("paper cuts") wasted tokens re-sending the static
envelope; long runs ("whales") accumulated large uncached conversation
histories.

## Changes

### Static envelope caching

- Hoist `systemInstruction`, `generationConfig`, `toolConfig` out of the while
  loop — built once, reused every turn
- Cache only SI + tools (no contents) before the loop starts, so every turn
  including turn 0 benefits from caching
- Build the request body conditionally: with cache → `cachedContent` +
  `contents.slice(cachedContentCount)`; without cache → full body

### Progressive cache refresh

- After each turn, compute uncached tokens from `usageMetadata`
  (`promptTokenCount - cachedContentTokenCount`)
- When uncached tokens exceed `RECACHE_THRESHOLD` (16,384), create a new cache
  with SI + tools + conversation contents (minus the last entry to avoid empty
  `contents` on the next turn)
- Old caches expire naturally (1hr TTL)

### Results

- Short runs: **93% cache hit rate** (39k/42k tokens cached)
- Long runs: **71% cache hit rate**, net input reduced from 150k to 57k tokens
  (~62% reduction)

## Testing

- Run an agent with `ENABLE_CONTEXT_CACHING=true`
- Short run: verify `cachedContentTokenCount` appears in usage metadata on all
  turns
- Long run: verify progressive refresh kicks in (multiple cache creations) and
  net input stays low
- Run with `ENABLE_CONTEXT_CACHING=false` to verify normal behavior is unchanged

author: codybingham
body:
### Motivation
- Provide the nonlinear solving pipeline required by ROADMAP Task F so the core can find solutions to parsed `Program` equations, report convergence status, and call into the property facade without tying tests to CoolProp.

### Description
- Add a new `core::solver` module implementing `solve_program`/`solve_program_with_options` and types `ConvergenceReport`, `ConvergenceStatus`, `SolveError`, `SolveOptions`, and `SolveResult` and re-export them from `core::lib`.
- Deterministically extract equations and known constants from a `Program` using the heuristic that direct numeric or quantity assignments are known constants and all other identifiers are unknowns, and filter constant assignments out of the equation list (`is_constant_assignment`, `extract_known_constants`, `extract_equations`).
- Implement an `Expr -> f64` evaluator with support for `+ - * / ^`, unary `+/-`, grouping, math functions (`sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `exp`, `ln/log`, `sqrt`, `abs`), and property facade wrappers (`h`, `s`, `rho`, `t_from_ph`, `p_from_th`) that call through a `PropsProvider` (works with `MockPropsProvider`).
- Implement Newton-style iterations with a finite-difference Jacobian, a simple Gaussian elimination linear solve, damped line-search (halving `alpha`) to ensure residual norm reduction, variable scaling (`max(|x|, 1)`), and stopping criteria (residual norm, step norm, and max iterations). The solver returns a solution map and a `ConvergenceReport` listing iterations, final norm, status, and per-equation worst residuals with source spans.
- Add unit tests under `core/tests/solver.rs` covering linear 2x2 solve, nonlinear solve (`x^2 = 2`), property-call equation solved with `MockPropsProvider` fallback, damping recovery from poor initial guesses, and clean error/reporting for underdetermined/inconsistent systems.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo fmt` to format changes (success).
- Ran `cargo test` and all core tests including the new solver tests passed (linear, nonlinear, property-call, damping recovery, invalid-system reporting all succeeded).
- Ran `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and fixed lints so clippy completed with no warnings (success).

author: rrlamichhane
body:
## Summary

This PR has grown to include three related sets of improvements:

### 1. Review workflow: failure recovery step
- Adds a `Post failure notice` step to both `claude-review-internal` and `claude-review-oss` jobs in `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml`
- Runs only when the `claude-review` step fails (`if: failure() && steps.claude-review.outcome == 'failure'`)
- Posts a PR comment explaining the review was interrupted and that any inline comments above are still valid findings
- Tells the user they can re-trigger with `/claude-review`
- Addresses the gap where a timeout or error leaves orphaned inline comments with no summary or closure

### 2. Bash validator: heredoc-aware command splitting
- `split_commands()` now detects `<< DELIM` and `<<- DELIM` heredoc operators
- Heredoc body content is consumed as an atomic chunk and not split on `&&`, `||`, `;`, or newlines
- Prevents false splits on commands like `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'\n...\nEOF\n)"` and `python3 - << 'PYEOF'\n...\nPYEOF`
- `_parse_heredoc_delim()` parses all heredoc forms: `<<DELIM`, `<<'DELIM'`, `<<"DELIM"`, `<<-DELIM`, `<<-'DELIM'`

### 3. Bash validator: correct `<<` vs `<<-` delimiter semantics
- `_parse_heredoc_delim()` now returns a 3-tuple `(delim, strip_tabs, end_pos)` instead of 2-tuple
- Regular `<<`: delimiter line must match exactly (no leading whitespace stripped)
- `<<-`: only leading **tabs** are stripped from the delimiter line before comparing (bash semantics — spaces are NOT stripped)
- Fixes a bug where `.strip()` was used for both forms, causing space-indented delimiter lines to incorrectly close regular `<<` heredocs

### 4. Bash validator: `$()` command substitution consumed atomically
- `$()` substitutions are now consumed as a single chunk in `split_commands()`
- Prevents false splits inside `$()` bodies (e.g., `echo "$(git log --oneline -5)"` no longer splits on spaces)
- Works in unquoted context and inside double quotes; correctly skipped inside single quotes
- `_find_matching_paren()` helper tracks nested parens and quote context within `$()`

### 5. Bash validator: additional shell builtins in allow list
- Added `continue [N]`, `break [N]`, `shift [N]` (loop control)
- Added `unset`, `readonly`, `typeset`, `let`, `getopts`, `builtin`, `hash` (variable/function builtins)
- All new patterns have corresponding test cases in `tests/bash-test-cases.toml`

## Test plan

- [x] Full CI-equivalent passes locally: shellcheck, TOML validation, pytest (560 tests), shell integration (481 tests), manage-agents tests
- [x] Heredoc content not split: `python3 - << 'PYEOF'\n...\nPYEOF` → allow
- [x] `<<-` tab-stripping: tab-indented delimiter closes, space-indented does not
- [x] Regular `<<` exact match: space-indented delimiter does not close
- [x] Dangerous commands still blocked through heredocs: `sudo cat << EOF\n...\nEOF` → deny
- [x] `$()` atomic: `echo "$(git log --oneline -5)"` → allow (no false splits)
- [x] New builtins: `continue`, `break 2`, `shift`, `unset MY_VAR`, `let x=1+2`, `hash -r` → allow
- [ ] Review failure: trigger a review that times out and verify the failure notice appears
- [ ] Successful review: verify no failure notice is posted

author: chesars
body:
## Relevant issues

Fixes context overflow issues for Claude Code users on Bedrock — the `/v1/messages/count_tokens` proxy endpoint was discarding `system` and `tools`, returning artificially low token counts (e.g. 10 instead of 531 with 3 tools).

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

The proxy's `/v1/messages/count_tokens` endpoint and all provider token counters (Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure AI) only passed `messages` to the token counting APIs, silently discarding `system` prompts and `tools`. This caused clients like Claude Code to receive incorrect token counts, preventing proper context window management and leading to context overflow errors.

**Example:** A request with 1 message + system prompt + 3 MCP tools returns **10 tokens** (bug) instead of **531 tokens** (correct).

### Fix

Pass `system` and `tools` through the full token counting chain:

1. **`TokenCountRequest`** — added `tools` and `system` fields
2. **`proxy/anthropic_endpoints/endpoints.py`** — extract `tools`/`system` from request body
3. **`proxy/proxy_server.py`** — pass them to provider counters
4. **`BaseTokenCounter` interface** — added `tools`/`system` parameters
5. **Bedrock** — transform tools to `toolConfig` format, system to text blocks
6. **Anthropic / Azure AI** — pass through directly (same API format)
7. **Gemini / Vertex AI** — accept `**kwargs` for forward compatibility

### Tests

- 8 new Bedrock transformation tests (system as string/list, tools, combined, sanitization)
- 5 new Anthropic transformation tests (system, tools, combined, none)
- All 19 count_tokens tests passing

body:
Extends `LogWriter` in `ServerSafeReboot.Remediation.ps1` to write structured entries to the Windows Event Log in addition to the existing file log.

## Changes

### Script Parameters
- `$EventLogName` (default: `Application`) — target event log
- `$EventLogSource` (default: `ServerSafeReboot`) — event source name

### LogWriter Class
- **Properties:** `EventLogName`, `EventSource`, per-type running event ID counters (`InfoEventId` starting at 1000, `WarnEventId` at 2000, `ErrorEventId` at 3000)
- **New constructor overload:** accepts `Path`, `EventLogName`, `EventSource`
- **`EnsureEventSource()`** — creates the source if absent; failures (e.g. no elevation) fall back to the file log via `Write()`
- **`WriteInfoEvent()` / `WriteWarnEvent()` / `WriteErrorEvent()`** — each calls `EnsureEventSource()`, writes the entry with the current counter ID, increments the counter, and catches write failures to the file log

### Pre-Reboot Event
An Information event is written immediately before `Restart-Computer`, recording both the initiating script and the joined pending reasons:

```powershell
$eventMessage = "ServerSafeReboot: Reboot initiated by this script. Pending reasons: $($pendingReasons -join ', ')"
$Logger.WriteInfoEvent($eventMessage)
```

body:
Adds a general-purpose `:::database` WMD component that renders a live-filtered table from an external JSON data file. First use: Latin vocabulary lookup on the Latin article (search English → Latin or Latin → definition).

## Component

**WMD syntax:**
```
:::database Latin Vocabulary | data/latin-vocab.json
:::
```

**Data file shape** (`data/*.json`):
```json
{
  "columns": [
    { "key": "latin",   "label": "Latin"          },
    { "key": "english", "label": "English"         },
    { "key": "pos",     "label": "Part of Speech"  },
    { "key": "notes",   "label": "Notes"           }
  ],
  "rows": [
    { "latin": "amare", "english": "to love", "pos": "verb (1st conj.)", "notes": "amo, amare, amavi, amatum" }
  ]
}
```

Search filters all columns simultaneously; lowercase values are pre-computed at load time for performance.

## Changes

- **`wmd-parser.js`** — `renderDatabaseBlock()` renderer + `case 'database':` in block switch
- **`scripts.js`** — `initDatabases()`: fetches JSON, pre-builds search index, wires `input` event for live filtering
- **`styles.css`** — `.wiki-database` styles: primary-colored header bar, inline search input, striped table, entry count, loading/empty states
- **`data/latin-vocab.json`** — 142 entries across verbs (all conjugations + irregular), nouns (3 declensions), adjectives, conjunctions, adverbs, prepositions
- **`articles/latin.wmd`** — new "Latin Vocabulary Reference" section using `:::database`
- **`AI_INSTRUCTIONS.txt`** — `:::database` documented in Section 4 with JSON spec and usage guidance
- **`admin/components-guide.wmd`** — new section with syntax, format spec, and live demo instance

author: koothodilabhijithaugustine
body:
# Description

Resolves #395 and #413

This draft PR introduces a complete tutorial and a set of supporting Python tools for performing **phase-resolved pulsar analysis** within the `cosipy` framework. 

Currently, the workflow demonstrates how to process Data Challenge 2 (DC2) FITS data for the Crab pulsar and its corresponding albedo background. The end goal of this pipeline is to prepare isolated on-pulse and off-pulse FITS files that are ready for downstream COSI Spectral Fitting.

### Key Additions
* **Phase-Resolved Analysis Tutorial (`example_notebook.ipynb`)**: A step-by-step Jupyter Notebook guiding users through combining unbinned data, slicing by Mission Elapsed Time (MET), assigning phases, plotting the pulse profile, and selecting phase intervals.
* **`phase_assigner.py`**: A new module that reads a pulsar ephemeris file (e.g., `crab.par`) and calculates/appends the exact rotational phase to individual photon events in a FITS file.
* **`plot_pulse_profile.py`**: A plotting utility to generate and visualize the folded light curve/pulse profile from the phase-assigned data.
* **`phase_selector.py`**: A filtering tool to extract specific phase windows (e.g., on-pulse and off-pulse regions) and save them as new FITS files.

body:
<!-- Describe the intention of the changes being proposed. What problem does it solve or functionality does it add? -->

- From testing I noticed that route patterns defined for a fragment can be seen as split into two categories
  1. Request to the main index.html file of the fragment
  2. Subsequent requests to get any additional asset of the fragment
which can also be seen in different examples when registering fragments into the gateway where there is a unique route pattern (often prefixed by a namespace such as /__wf/<fragment-id>) which matches a baseHref defined in the fragment index.html and is used for requests of category 2., and a route pattern that matches the path where the fragment is expected to load in the host app (assuming the fragment is loaded as route-bound) with purpose of retrieving the index.html of the fragment (category 1.).
The concern  with this approach is that the fragment gateway has to be aware of routes defined in the host app making it more difficult to render a fragment with a unique id anywhere in the app. 
With the following [change](https://github.com/web-fragments/web-fragments/commit/f5b7702c6c96c16713d61502fa264a11bfde978d), when matching fragment config know also checks that, if provided (which is done so in the request of category 1.), the fragmentId header also matches one of the fragment configs of matched route patter, but in this case we would not need to check that the request path matches a routePattern of a fragment since we can already uniquely identify the fragment of the given id (assuming i exists, otherwise we default to know match), which is exactly what we propose doing with the change. The final result of this would allow removing dependency of the fragment gateway to routes defined in the host webapp and enable loading fragments anywhere given a corresponding fragmentId

author: copilot
body:
Fatal crash (`java.util.concurrent.CancellationException: Task was cancelled`) in `AudioServiceConnectionKt$await$2$1.run`, observed predominantly on Google Pixel devices. Two cooperating bugs cause this:

1. **`ExecutionException` not unwrapped** — `MediaController.buildAsync()` on Google's Media3 can wrap `java.util.concurrent.CancellationException` inside `ExecutionException`. The `await` extension only caught the direct `FutureCancellationException`, so the wrapped case fell to `catch (e: Exception)` → `continuation.resumeWithException(executionException)`, failing the coroutine as a regular exception rather than a cancellation.

2. **No `CoroutineExceptionHandler` on `controllerScope`** — `SupervisorJob()` isolates child failures but without a handler they still reach the thread's `UncaughtExceptionHandler` → fatal crash.

## Changes

- **`await` extension**: Added explicit `catch (e: ExecutionException)` that unwraps `e.cause`; if it's a `FutureCancellationException`, calls `continuation.cancel(...)` instead of `resumeWithException`.

```kotlin
} catch (e: ExecutionException) {
    val cause = e.cause
    if (cause is FutureCancellationException) {
        continuation.cancel(CancellationException("ListenableFuture was cancelled", cause))
    } else {
        continuation.resumeWithException(cause ?: e)
    }
}
```

- **`controllerScope`**: Added `CoroutineExceptionHandler` that logs via `Log.e` and swallows to prevent non-cancellation exceptions from crashing the app.

author: dev-doshi
body:
## Summary
`BitcoinTransaction::TotalInputsAmount()` and `TotalOutputsAmount()` sum `uint64_t` values with unchecked `+=`. With enough crafted UTXOs, the sum can silently overflow, causing `EffectiveFeeAmount()` (which subtracts them) and `AmountsAreValid()` to produce incorrect results.

Cardano already uses `base::CheckedNumeric<uint64_t>` for the same pattern. ZCash PR #34260 also addresses this for ZCash.

## Fix
Replace raw `uint64_t` accumulation with `base::CheckedNumeric<uint64_t>` and call `ValueOrDie()` (which CHECK-fails on overflow rather than silently wrapping).

## Severity
**Low-Medium** — silent integer overflow in transaction amount calculation.

Resolves brave/brave-browser#53248

author: kristjanesperanto
body:
On iOS Chrome and other WKWebView-based browsers, `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission()` can reject, causing an unhandled promise rejection in the console. This PR adds proper error handling and refactors the compass logic into dedicated methods.

Note: The underlying geolocation issue on iOS Chrome (#334) is a platform limitation that cannot be fixed in JavaScript. It may no longer occur on newer iOS versions — no new reports have been filed since 2023.

## Changes

### Error handling

- Wrap `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission()` in `try/catch` so permission errors are caught and logged as a warning instead of producing unhandled rejections.

### Refactoring

- Extract `_activateCompass()` — compass setup (feature detection, permission request, event binding) in its own `async` method. Removes `const _this = this`, nested function declaration, and deep nesting.
- Extract `_deactivateCompass()` — symmetric counterpart for cleanup.
- Store bound event name in `_compassEventName` instead of re-running feature detection in `_deactivate()`.

### Tests

- 12 new tests covering compass activation and deactivation (permission granted/denied/rejected, feature detection, event binding/unbinding, cleanup).

## Breaking changes

None.

author: ichoosetoaccept
body:
## What

Replaces all per-request `gh` CLI subprocess calls with a direct GitHub REST/GraphQL client built on `httpx`. Token is resolved once at startup (env var → `gh auth token` fallback) and reused for every request.

## Why

- **Fixes subprocess hang bug** (#65): `gh` CLI calls block the event loop and were the root cause of the MCP server becoming unresponsive under load.
- **Eliminates `cwd` dependency**: `gh` used the working directory to detect the repo; `httpx` calls use an explicit `repo` parameter or a one-time `gh` fallback, so the server no longer needs a workspace root.
- **Unblocks PAT migration** (#85): The new `github_api.py` layer is the foundation for switching to fine-grained PATs and removing the `gh` CLI runtime dependency entirely.

## Changes

### New: `src/codereviewbuddy/github_api.py`
- `GitHubError` / `GitHubAuthError` exception hierarchy
- `parse_repo()` — splits `owner/repo` strings
- `get_token()` — resolves token once (GH_TOKEN → GITHUB_TOKEN → `gh auth token`), raises `GitHubAuthError` with a magic PAT-creation URL if none found
- `graphql()` — cached GraphQL queries, cache-busting mutations
- `rest()` — cached GET requests, paginated REST with `Link:` header following
- `download_bytes()` — for CI log zip downloads

### Migrated callers
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tools/comments.py` | All `gh.graphql`/`gh.rest` → `await github_api.graphql`/`rest`; internal functions made `async` |
| `tools/stack.py` | Same; `_fetch_merged_prs`, `_fetch_pr_summary`, `_fetch_open_prs` now `async` |
| `tools/issues.py` | `create_issue_from_comment` now `async` |
| `tools/descriptions.py` | `_fetch_pr_info` now `async` |
| `server.py` | `await` added to calls that became `async` |

### Tests
- `tests/test_github_api.py` — new; covers token resolution, error types, REST/GraphQL/paginate/download via `respx` mocks
- `tests/test_comments.py`, `test_stack.py`, `test_issues.py` — updated to `AsyncMock`, correct `github_api.*` patch paths, `await` on async calls

## What's not changed yet (follow-up phases)
- `gh.get_repo_info` and `gh.get_current_pr_number` still used as sync fallbacks (wrapped in `asyncio.to_thread`) — Phase 3 will replace these with git + API
- `server.py` workspace detection still present — Phase 4 will simplify
- `ci.py` still uses `gh` for log fetching — Phase 5

Closes #65
Related to #85

author: gmartin-dev
body:
# Trace-derived eval workflow (collect/export + dataset evaluate) ## What Is New ### `penguiflow eval` command group - `penguiflow eval collect --spec ...` - runs query cases, captures traces, exports a minimal dataset bundle - writes: `dataset.jsonl` + `manifest.json` - `penguiflow eval evaluate --spec ...` - evaluates an existing dataset bundle - supports baseline-only mode or candidate sweep mode - runs in-memory by default (no workspace artifacts) - optionally writes one JSON report when `report_path` is set ### Public eval API surface (`penguiflow.evals`) - `collect_traces()` - `collect_and_export_traces()` - `export_dataset()` - `evaluate_dataset()` - `evaluate_dataset_from_spec_file()` - `load_eval_collect_spec()` / `load_eval_dataset_spec()` ### Data/eval behavior improvements - baseline-only evaluation when `candidates_path` is omitted - candidate sweep ranking + holdout regression gate when candidates are provided - optional `min_test_score` gate for CI policy thresholds - strict candidate validation (ids, patch shape, duplicate patch detection) - support for trace references across sessions via typed `TraceRef` --- ## Why This Matters Before this change, teams had strong trace/debug tooling but no first-class eval workflow. After this change, teams can run a stable quality loop from committed specs: - **reproducible**: pinned dataset inputs and explicit specs - **pragmatic**: minimal default outputs, human-readable summaries - **extensible**: project-owned metrics and run hooks via import paths - **safe for CI**: holdout regression checks + optional minimum score gates --- ## Usage Examples ### 1) Collect and pin dataset ```bash uv run penguiflow eval collect \ --spec examples/planner_enterprise_agent_v2/evals/policy_compliance_v1/collect.spec.json ``` ### 2) Re-evaluate pinned dataset ```bash uv run penguiflow eval evaluate \ --spec examples/planner_enterprise_agent_v2/evals/policy_compliance_v1/evaluate.spec.json ``` ### 3) Metric callable contract ```python def metric(gold, pred, trace=None, pred_name=None, pred_trace=None): ... ``` --- ## Output Contract (Intentional) | Command | Default output | |---|---| | `eval collect` | `dataset.jsonl`, `manifest.json` | | `eval evaluate` | stdout summary only | Optional: - set `report_path` in evaluate spec to emit one JSON report file --- ## Included Example Bundle End-to-end baseline-first example: - `examples/planner_enterprise_agent_v2/evals/policy_compliance_v1/README.md` - query suite + collect/evaluate specs - pinned dataset + manifest - deterministic trace-aware policy metric This serves as the reference path for real project adoption. --- ## Validation and Coverage This PR adds targeted tests for: - collect/evaluate spec loading and path resolution - dataset export structure and contracts - baseline-only execution flow - candidate ranking + holdout regression behavior - `min_test_score` gating - optional single-report write behavior --- ## Reviewer Guide If you only review a few files: - CLI behavior: `penguiflow/cli/main.py`, `docs/cli/eval-command.md` - API surface: `penguiflow/evals/api.py`, `penguiflow/evals/__init__.py` - Trace export/evidence: `penguiflow/evals/export.py` - Eval runner semantics: `penguiflow/evals/runner.py` - Example adoption path: `examples/planner_enterprise_agent_v2/evals/policy_compliance_v1/README.md` ---
Operational Notes - Relative path resolution is canonicalized around `project_root` when present. - Env files from spec are loaded first; CLI `--env-file` overrides are loaded after. - Existing process env values are preserved (not overwritten). - Candidate-free runs are first-class (baseline-only mode).

author: ludovicsanchez38-creator
body:
## Summary
- Sur Linux .deb, `resource_dir()` renvoie `/usr/lib/THERESE/` mais les fichiers backend sont dans `/usr/lib/THERESE/binaries/backend-libs/`
- Le join dans `lib.rs` faisait `.join("backend-libs")` au lieu de `.join("binaries").join("backend-libs")`
- Résultat : le sidecar wrapper échouait avec `exec: /usr/lib/THERESE/backend-libs/backend: not found`

## Cause
`tauri.linux.conf.json` déclare les resources avec le prefix `binaries/` :
```json
"resources": ["binaries/backend-libs/*", "binaries/backend-libs/_internal/**/*"]
```
Tauri préserve cette structure dans le .deb, donc le chemin complet est `{resource_dir}/binaries/backend-libs/`.

## Correctif
`lib.rs` ligne 311 : `.join("backend-libs")` -> `.join("binaries").join("backend-libs")`

## Test
Testé sur DreamQuest Ludo (Ubuntu 24.04, .deb v0.4.5) - le backend démarre correctement après ce fix (appliqué via symlink).

### Motivation
- Mobile users reported the initial language wasn't selected according to geolocation and the menu indicator could appear unaligned or not visibly active.
- The goal is to pick the correct initial language by country when there is no saved preference and make the active language clearly visible in the mobile menu.

### Description
- Added utility functions `mapCountryToLang`, `mapBrowserLangToLang`, `detectInitialLanguage` and `refreshActiveLanguageIndicator` to derive the initial language from geolocation (via `https://ipapi.co/json/`) with a safe fallback to `navigator.language`.
- Switched startup flow to asynchronous initialization using `detectInitialLanguage().then(...)` and invoke `applyLanguage` with the detected language.
- Ensured the language indicator is recalculated when the mobile menu opens and on window `resize` by calling `refreshActiveLanguageIndicator`, preventing the indicator from getting stuck when the menu is hidden.
- Improved visual emphasis for the active button by strengthening `.lang-switch .active` styling and applied identical edits to both `index.min.html` and `public/index.min.html` for consistency.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

WorkManager's `SystemForegroundService` crashes on Android 14+ with `IllegalArgumentException: foregroundServiceType 0x00000001 is not a subset of foregroundServiceType attribute 0x00000000` when `OfflineDownloadWorker` calls `setForeground(ForegroundInfo(..., FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC))`. The manifest already declared `foregroundServiceType="dataSync"` on the service, but without `tools:node="merge"` the manifest merger silently drops the attribute when combining the app declaration with WorkManager's own library manifest entry — leaving the final merged manifest with type `0x00000000`.

**Fix:** add `tools:node="merge"` so the merger explicitly combines the app's `foregroundServiceType` attribute onto WorkManager's existing service element:

```xml
<!-- Before -->
<service
    android:name="androidx.work.impl.foreground.SystemForegroundService"
    android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />

<!-- After -->
<service
    android:name="androidx.work.impl.foreground.SystemForegroundService"
    android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync"
    tools:node="merge" />
```

author: copilot
body:
The `bump-and-release` workflow failed while computing the next version because marketplace metadata JSON was passed to `node -e` as a positional argument, exceeding OS argument-length limits. This change keeps the release logic intact but makes JSON parsing robust to large payloads.

- **Workflow reliability: version parsing path**
  - In `release-version-bump.yml`, changed marketplace JSON parsing from `process.argv[1]` to stdin-based parsing.
  - This removes dependence on shell/OS argv limits while preserving existing extraction logic (`versions[0].version || version`).

- **Behavior preserved**
  - Version selection and bump behavior are unchanged.
  - Only the transport mechanism for JSON into Node was updated.

```yaml
# before
MARKETPLACE_VERSION=$(node -e "...JSON.parse(process.argv[1])..." "$MARKETPLACE_JSON")

# after
MARKETPLACE_VERSION=$(printf '%s' "$MARKETPLACE_JSON" | node -e "const fs = require('fs'); const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8')); ...")
```

8 new optional `str | None` fields (all `None` by default — fully backward compatible):
| Env var | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `SYSTEM_PROMPT` | Global base prepended to all prompts |
| `SYSTEM_PROMPT_SUFFIX` | Appended to global base |
| `CODING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` | Full override of coding prompt |

| `MR_COMMENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_SUFFIX` | Appended to default MR comment prompt |

### Modified: consumers
- `coding_engine.py` — uses `get_prompt(settings, "coding")`
- `review_engine.py` — uses `get_prompt(settings, "review")`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT` → `REVIEW_SYSTEM_PROMPT`
- `mr_comment_handler.py` — uses `get_prompt(settings, "mr_comment")`
- `task_runner.py` — uses `get_prompt()` for both task types

### #191 fix applied
Default coding prompt now says: follow existing conventions for style/formatting/architecture, but always prioritize repo-defined security standards over patterns in existing code.

### Documentation updated
- `docs/wiki/task-execution.md` — updated System Prompts section with new module references, added Prompt Configurability subsection with env var table and resolution order
- `docs/wiki/module-reference.md` — added `prompt_defaults.py` module entry, updated `review_engine.py` (`SYSTEM_PROMPT` → `REVIEW_SYSTEM_PROMPT`), `coding_engine.py` (re-export noted), `mr_comment_handler.py` and `task_runner.py` imports

**Finding: Global prompt suffix dropped when global prompt is set** — Severity: Medium
- `get_prompt()` originally ignored `system_prompt_suffix` when `system_prompt` was set, contradicting the field description
- **Fixed**: global layer now concatenates both values (no built-in default to "replace", so override+suffix should combine)
- Test updated to assert the combined behavior

No other findings.

~406 insertions / ~122 deletions. Most insertions are prompt text moved from existing files + doc updates, not net new logic.

author: anthonyshew
body:
## Summary

- OTEL metrics are now sent whenever `experimentalObservability.otel` is configured, without requiring `--summarize`

## Problem

`RunTracker::finish()` has a fast-path optimization that skips the expensive `RunSummary` construction (task summaries, SCM state via git subprocesses) when neither `--dry` nor `--summarize` is passed. Since OTEL metrics are recorded inside `RunSummary::finish()`, this early return meant OTEL was silently never fired in normal runs — even when fully configured.

## Fix

Added `&& self.observability_handle.is_none()` to the early-return guard. When OTEL is configured, the code falls through to the full `RunSummary` path where `handle.record()` and `handle.shutdown()` are called. The fast path is preserved for the common case (no OTEL, no `--summarize`, no `--dry`).

## What Changed

1. Dataset workflow and governance

- Prevents leaked process resources/semaphore warnings under fast worker exits.

author: scotwells
body:
## Summary

Enables automatic Activity generation from Kubernetes Events. When something happens in your cluster (pod crashes, deployments roll out, config changes), the processor translates these events into human-readable Activity summaries.

## What's New

### Event Processing Pipeline

Events flow through this pipeline:
```
K8s Events → Event Exporter → NATS → Activity Processor → Activities
```

The processor evaluates events against ActivityPolicy `eventRules` using CEL expressions to generate summaries like:
- "Pod api-server-xyz crashed with OOMKilled"
- "Deployment frontend rolled out successfully"
- "ConfigMap updated by alice@example.com"

### Dead Letter Queue

Failed events don't get lost—they go to a DLQ for later retry:
- Configurable retry policies
- Metrics for monitoring DLQ depth
- Manual inspection via NATS tooling

### K8s Event Exporter

New component that watches cluster events and publishes to NATS:
- Supports both core/v1 and events.k8s.io/v1 formats
- Exports metrics for monitoring event flow
- Deploys as a separate pod in activity-system

### Bug Fix

- Fixed ClickHouse table name in Vector config (`audit_logs` not `events`)

## Why This Matters

- **Unified Timeline**: Events and audit logs together in one Activity feed
- **Reliable Processing**: DLQ ensures no events are silently dropped
- **Customizable**: Write CEL rules to translate events your way
- **Observable**: Metrics for processing lag, errors, and throughput

## Test Plan
- [ ] Deploy to dev cluster
- [ ] Verify k8s-event-exporter pod is running
- [ ] Create a pod and verify event appears in Activity feed
- [ ] Verify DLQ metrics are exposed
- [ ] Test failure scenario and verify event lands in DLQ

## Dependencies

- Requires #66 (Events API) - ✅ Merged
- Requires #67 (Observability) - ✅ Merged

## Related

- Enhancement: https://github.com/datum-cloud/enhancements/issues/469

When set_cell writes a value via nexsInteract the server-side session updates immediately, but the NExS iframe only redraws if it receives an {op:"input"} postMessage.  The existing ontoolresult path doesn't fire reliably in all host environments (e.g. ChatGPT may not propagate app-tool results to the App View for non-render tools).

New mechanism:
- NexsSession gains a pendingDisplayInputs queue.
- set_cell pushes {viewIndex, addr, value} to that queue after every successful nexsInteract call.
- New internal tool pop_nexs_display_inputs (visibility: ["app"]) returns and clears the queue.
- The browser runs a 1-second setInterval that drains the queue via callServerTool and sends each entry to the iframe as {op:"input"}, which triggers the iframe's own recalculation and redraws the cell.

The ontoolresult fast path (zero delay) is preserved; the polling loop is a fallback that guarantees the display syncs within ~1 second even when ontoolresult doesn't fire.

author: uatec
body:
Dispatcher.UIThread.Post is fire-and-forget: each provider task was
completing (and being seen as done by Task.WhenAll) before its UI
callback actually ran. For slow providers like YouTube (which spawns
yt-dlp), this meant the final sort + UpdateSearchResultRows() call
finished before YouTube's results were committed to SearchResults.
The pip count was set correctly (inside the same late-running Post),
but SearchResultRows was never rebuilt, so nothing rendered.

Switching to await Dispatcher.UIThread.InvokeAsync ensures each
provider task only completes once its results are genuinely in
SearchResults. Task.WhenAll then guarantees that UpdateSearchResultRows
sees the full result set from every provider.

<!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag leads as needed. -->

### Explanation of Change

Fixes a regression from #83432 where navigating from "Review Duplicates" to `SEARCH_REPORT` caused wrong prev/next arrow state on first open.

**Root cause:** After removing `useDeepCompareRef`, the effect in `MoneyRequestReportTransactionList` used `visualOrderTransactionIDs` directly as its dependency. When navigating to `SEARCH_REPORT`, Onyx data loads triggered `useMemo` recomputation, producing a new array reference with the same (or slightly different) content. This caused the effect to re-fire and overwrite the transaction IDs set by `TransactionDuplicateReview.onPreviewPressed`, placing the clicked transaction at the wrong position in the list.

**Fix:** Use a `join(',')` primitive string key as the effect dependency. The effect only re-fires when the array content actually changes, matching the original `useDeepCompareRef` behavior without the deep-equal overhead or React Compiler incompatibility. The idempotent guard in `setActiveTransactionIDs` stays as a defense-in-depth layer.

### Motivation
- Prevent infinite/very frequent `history.replaceState` calls caused by URL sync during slide drags which leads to "Attempt to use history.replaceState() more than 100 times" and UI crashes.
- Restore correct Back navigation so closing a part card returns to the previous screen without landing on an empty/errored route.
- Prevent a failing `sw.js` registration from producing an unhandled promise rejection and breaking the UI.

### Description
- Refactored vendor slider URL sync to separate transient and committed slide state (`transientDragIndex` / `committedIndex`) so the URL is updated only for the committed (settled) slide index and not on every drag; added a 300ms debounce and guards to skip writes when the computed query equals the current location.
- Made part-card navigation explicitly use router push semantics (`navigate(..., { replace: false })`) so the browser Back behaves predictably and does not participate in replace loops.
- Wrapped `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js')` with `.catch(...)` in `index.tsx` to log registration failures and avoid unhandled promise rejections that could crash the UI when `sw.js` is missing or fails to load.
- Enhanced `SupplierSlidesErrorBoundary` with a non-destructive recovery UI by adding `Reload slide` and `Copy debug` controls that clear the boundary state and emit a debug payload to the clipboard/logs for diagnostics.

author: keithamus
body:
This change significantly rewrites the Lexer to use a ByteCursor struct instead
of Chars. This is useful for 2 reasons: 1. Chars can be a little slower than
comparing bytes, when we know the input to be UTF-8, but more importantly 2.
With a slice of bytes we can start using memchr, which uses SIMD operations so
we don't have to, and switching between Bytes/Chars hampers the performance
benefits of using memchr.

During this rewrite I also picked up a couple of other chances for optimisation,
such as fast-path integer parsing, and improving the scanning of
strings/URLs/comments, plus a bunch of small changes like inline hints.

This change is purely performance oriented, and functionality should be
identical.
